item.title: Kentucky and Louisiana set to play at Blue Wahoos Stadium in 2027
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The game marks another high-profile event for the downtown Pensacola venue, which has hosted various collegiate and professional sporting…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos announced Thursday that Blue Wahoos Stadium will host a college baseball matchup between the University of Kentucky Wildcats and the University of Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns in 2027.

The game marks another high-profile event for the downtown Pensacola venue, which has hosted various collegiate and professional sporting events since opening. Details about the specific date and time for the Kentucky-Louisiana contest have not yet been announced.

The Blue Wahoos, Pensacola's minor league baseball team, regularly partner with event organizers to bring marquee matchups to the community. The 2027 game will add to the stadium's growing calendar of non-baseball events that draw regional and national attention to the facility.

item.title: Blue Angels close 2026 season with finale at NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Navy's Blue Angels wrapped up their 2026 performance schedule Saturday with a high-energy display at the NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show, drawing thousands of spectators to watch the elite flight demonstration team perform. The opening day of the air show featured the Blue Angels' signature precision flying and aerial maneuvers,…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Navy's Blue Angels wrapped up their 2026 performance schedule Saturday with a high-energy display at the NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show, drawing thousands of spectators to watch the elite flight demonstration team perform.

The opening day of the air show featured the Blue Angels' signature precision flying and aerial maneuvers, delivering what organizers called a "bang" to kick off the event at the base just north of Pensacola. The performance marked the team's final scheduled show of the year.

The NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show is a signature annual event that brings together military aviation displays, civilian aircraft, and crowds from across Northwest Florida and beyond. The show typically runs over multiple days and draws aviation enthusiasts and families to the base.

item.title: PPD Thanks Pensacola Voters for Approving Penny Sales Tax
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Police Department posted a video on Facebook thanking city residents for voting to approve the local option sales tax, according to WKRG News 5. The penny tax, which passed at the ballot on Tuesday, is expected to fund police operations and other city services. The department's thank-you message comes as the city moves forward with…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Police Department posted a video on Facebook thanking city residents for voting to approve the local option sales tax, according to WKRG News 5. The penny tax, which passed at the ballot on Tuesday, is expected to fund police operations and other city services. The department's thank-you message comes as the city moves forward with implementing the voter-approved measure.

The tax increase will add one cent to every dollar spent on taxable purchases in Pensacola. Police departments across Florida have increasingly turned to such ballot initiatives to secure stable funding for operations and staffing in recent years.

item.title: Multi-agency sweep nabs 6, seizes 2 pounds of fentanyl in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A coordinated law enforcement operation across Escambia County has resulted in six arrests and the seizure of a significant cache of drugs, weapons, and cash, according to North Escambia. The sweep, dubbed "Operation Lucky Charms," targeted drug trafficking activity throughout the county. Authorities recovered nearly two pounds of fentanyl along…
item.content:encoded:
A coordinated law enforcement operation across Escambia County has resulted in six arrests and the seizure of a significant cache of drugs, weapons, and cash, according to North Escambia.

The sweep, dubbed "Operation Lucky Charms," targeted drug trafficking activity throughout the county. Authorities recovered nearly two pounds of fentanyl along with firearms, vehicles, and more than $100,000 in cash during the operation.

Details about which agencies participated in the coordinated effort and the specific charges facing those arrested were not immediately available. The operation underscores ongoing law enforcement efforts to combat the opioid crisis and drug trafficking in the region.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida High School Athletic Association has announced its postseason football brackets for 2026, setting opening-round matchups across the Panhandle and state. State championship games for Classes 1A through 6A are scheduled for December 9–12 at South Dade Kia Field at Pitbull Stadium in Miami.

The brackets determine which teams advance to the playoffs and their path through the tournament. Details on specific Escambia County and Santa Rosa County playoff matchups were not included in the FHSAA's announcement, but local schools will begin playoff competition in the coming weeks as they pursue state titles.

The facility, slated for 7209 Lillian Highway, will be Fire Rescue's Station 11 and represents an expansion of emergency services capacity in the county. item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials held a groundbreaking Friday for a new fire station that will serve the Myrtle Grove area. The facility, slated for 7209 Lillian Highway, will be Fire Rescue's Station 11 and represents an expansion of emergency services capacity in the county.

Construction of the station marks the latest infrastructure investment by Escambia County Fire Rescue. The new facility is expected to improve response times and coverage for residents in the northern part of the county.

No timeline for completion was announced in the initial groundbreaking announcement.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is gearing up to host the Southeastern Conference Women's Soccer Tournament for the fifth straight year, with matches running Sunday through November 15 at Ashton Brosnaham Athletic Park in North Escambia.

The week-long event will bring together the SEC's top 12 women's soccer programs competing for the conference championship. The tournament draws regional and national attention to the area and represents a significant event for the local sports calendar.

This marks another year Escambia County has been selected as the host venue for one of the SEC's marquee postseason competitions, highlighting the quality facilities and infrastructure available in the North Escambia area.

item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola man has been arrested following an alleged arson incident in Escambia County in which a mobile home was deliberately set on fire with people inside, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies say the suspect also attempted to ignite a second trailer during the same incident. The arrest was made following the Thursday evening fire, which posed immediate danger to residents.

Details about potential charges, the suspect's identity, and the circumstances leading to the alleged arson remain under investigation. The Sheriff's Office has not released additional information about injuries or damage at this time.

item.content:encoded: Atmore Nursing Center recently received a donation of therapy dolls designed to help residents living with dementia, according to WKRG News 5. The donation highlights growing recognition in long-term care facilities of non-pharmaceutical interventions that can improve quality of life for residents with cognitive decline.

item.title: Blue Angels pilot Scott Laux removed from team
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Marine Corps Major Scott Laux has been removed from the Blue Angels, the Navy's elite flight demonstration squadron based at Naval Air Station Pensacola, according to the Chief of Naval Air Training. Laux, who served as the team's No. 6 opposing solo pilot, was dismissed "for failing to uphold the standards expected of members of the Navy Flight…
item.content:encoded:
Marine Corps Major Scott Laux has been removed from the Blue Angels, the Navy's elite flight demonstration squadron based at Naval Air Station Pensacola, according to the Chief of Naval Air Training.

Laux, who served as the team's No. 6 opposing solo pilot, was dismissed "for failing to uphold the standards expected of members of the Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron," according to a confirmation made to the Pensacola News Journal on November 6th. The removal is effective immediately.

The Blue Angels, formally known as the Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron, perform precision flying demonstrations worldwide and are headquartered at NAS Pensacola. The team maintains strict standards for its pilots both in and out of the cockpit. No additional details about the specific reasons for Laux's removal have been disclosed.

Park Place. Dogs and cats four months and older can receive rabies vaccines at no cost, and free microchips will also be available while…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Animal Welfare and the Florida Department of Health are hosting a free drive-through rabies vaccination clinic today from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the Escambia County Central Office Complex, 3363 W. Park Place.

Dogs and cats four months and older can receive rabies vaccines at no cost, and free microchips will also be available while supplies last. Pets must remain secured in vehicles during the clinic. County residents will need to bring valid photo identification.

Rabies vaccination is required by Escambia County law for all dogs and cats four months or older, with annual boosters needed. Proof of vaccination is required to obtain a county animal license. For questions, call the Department of Animal Welfare at 850-595-3075 or visit MyEscambia.com/animalwelfare.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola is inviting media to an off-camera briefing Monday, November 9 at 10 a.m. to discuss proposed updates to the city's tree ordinance ahead of a City Council presentation the following week.

City Arborist Mose Franklin and Wendy Gavin, manager of the Street and Traffic Operations Division, will walk through the revisions and explain the reasoning behind the changes. The briefing will be held in the Whibbs Conference Room on the first floor of City Hall, 222 W. Main St.

The proposed ordinance changes will then go before the full City Council for consideration. For more information, contact the City's Strategic Communications Office.

item.title: HUD Reports Largest Single-Year Drop in Homelessness Since Trump Took Office
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced today that homelessness declined 6.3% in the past year, according to the 2026 Point-in-Time count released by the agency. The count found 698,425 individuals homeless on a single night in January 2026, marking what HUD describes as the largest year-over-year decrease on record. HUD…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced today that homelessness declined 6.3% in the past year, according to the 2026 Point-in-Time count released by the agency. The count found 698,425 individuals homeless on a single night in January 2026, marking what HUD describes as the largest year-over-year decrease on record.

HUD Secretary Scott Turner attributed the decline to the Trump administration's border security policies and a Supreme Court ruling that affirmed local governments' authority to restrict encampments. The agency is shifting away from the "Housing First" approach implemented under the Biden administration, which HUD says correlated with a 28% increase in homelessness from 2022 to 2025, toward what it calls "Treatment First" policies that prioritize addressing addiction alongside housing assistance.

In July 2025, President Trump signed an executive order directing HUD to incorporate substance abuse treatment into homelessness programs as part of a broader public safety initiative. HUD received a record 3,700 applications for competitive homelessness funding announced in June and rolled out a "Best Practices Toolkit" on treating homelessness and addiction in August in partnership with the Department of Health and Human Services and the Office of National Drug Control Policy.

Despite the reported decline, HUD notes that homelessness remains near historic highs overall and that significant work remains to address the issue nationwide.

item.title: Disaster Relief Center Opens Saturday at Ferry Pass
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County will open a Disaster Multi-Agency Resource Center on Saturday, November 7 at 1 p.m. at the Ferry Pass Community Center to help residents and businesses recover from recent disaster damage. The center will operate daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and will have staff from FEMA, the State Emergency Response Team, and the Small Business…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County will open a Disaster Multi-Agency Resource Center on Saturday, November 7 at 1 p.m. at the Ferry Pass Community Center to help residents and businesses recover from recent disaster damage. The center will operate daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and will have staff from FEMA, the State Emergency Response Team, and the Small Business Administration ready to assist with recovery applications.

The SBA's Business Recovery Center, which shares the Ferry Pass location at 8800 N. 9th Ave., helps individuals and business owners navigate the agency's disaster loan program and complete applications for assistance. Walk-ins are welcome, though appointments can be scheduled in advance at appointment.sba.gov. Monday through Friday hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with Saturday hours from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The center will close for Thanksgiving on November 26 and Christmas on December 25, then permanently close at 5 p.m. on December 28.

Deadlines are critical: applications for physical property damage must be filed by December 28, while economic injury disaster loan applications are due by July 27, 2027. Residents and business owners can also apply online at sba.gov/disaster, call the SBA National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. Telecommunications relay services are available for people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability by dialing 7-1-1.

item.title: FDOT to resurface SR 89 in Milton; virtual update planned
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is holding a virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on State Road 89 (Dogwood Drive) between U.S. 90 and S.R. 87 in Milton. The roughly $20-million project will resurface existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, median crossovers, and paved shoulders. Beyond repaving, FDOT plans to upgrade…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is holding a virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on State Road 89 (Dogwood Drive) between U.S. 90 and S.R. 87 in Milton.

The roughly $20-million project will resurface existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, median crossovers, and paved shoulders. Beyond repaving, FDOT plans to upgrade pedestrian infrastructure to meet Americans with Disabilities Act standards, add buffered bike lanes, and improve traffic signals, signs, pavement markings, drainage, and lighting. No additional land acquisition will be needed.

Construction bids are scheduled for early 2028. Project details—including maps, drawings, and timelines—are available online at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/collections/18effe29792f49d9ae6f41f587c9c0e2. Residents can also contact project manager James Duvall at (850) 415-9021 or jduvall@hntb.com to review materials.

Public comments on the project update are due by Thursday, Dec. 10, 2026.

item.title: Escambia Extension's Lydia Purvis Named November Employee of the Month
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Lydia Purvis, a Horticulture Specialist with Escambia Extension Services, has been recognized as the county's November 2026 Employee of the Month. The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners honored Purvis with a proclamation at its November 5 meeting, citing her strong customer service, positive attitude, and collaborative approach to her…
item.content:encoded:
Lydia Purvis, a Horticulture Specialist with Escambia Extension Services, has been recognized as the county's November 2026 Employee of the Month. The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners honored Purvis with a proclamation at its November 5 meeting, citing her strong customer service, positive attitude, and collaborative approach to her work.

Since joining the Extension office in April 2022, Purvis has managed the Master Gardener Volunteer Program, handled community education about plants and horticulture, and created educational materials and videos for residents. Her role focuses on supporting UF/IFAS Extension's horticulture program while answering public questions about gardening and plant care. Extension Services Director Nick Simmons praised her ability to build relationships across the department and with the public. "She has worked hard to build positive relationships with our clients and staff and brings a can-do attitude to every task she manages," Simmons said in a statement.

Over the past year, Purvis coordinated "Traveling Through Extension," a new community outreach program that brought 135 third-grade students and teachers to the Extension office for educational field trips. The event featured six sessions on topics including animal interactions, food safety, healthy snacks, and plant growth. Purvis secured funding, worked with local schools, and coordinated volunteer efforts to make the program successful.

Purvis, a native of Escambia County, volunteers with several community organizations including Future Farmers of America, 4-H, and her church. She expressed gratitude for the recognition and her Extension team. "Every day in Extension is a new adventure," she said. "My favorite part is helping educate the public about the importance of horticulture."

item.title: Pensacola resumes curbside recycling; FEMA documentation critical for reimbursement
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Curbside recycling service has resumed in Pensacola following disruptions, according to city staff announcements. However, officials are emphasizing the importance of detailed record-keeping as the city pursues Federal Emergency Management Agency reimbursement for disaster-related costs. The advisory comes as Pensacola works through post-disaster…
item.content:encoded:
Curbside recycling service has resumed in Pensacola following disruptions, according to city staff announcements. However, officials are emphasizing the importance of detailed record-keeping as the city pursues Federal Emergency Management Agency reimbursement for disaster-related costs.

The advisory comes as Pensacola works through post-disaster recovery procedures. Staff have flagged that meticulous documentation will be essential to support any FEMA claims related to the interruption and resumption of waste management services.

Residents should continue to follow normal recycling guidelines as service returns to regular schedules.
